brief_summary: Two-column ledger, four cards per column. Left column ('hot-swap', coral-filled cards) lists: tool-free switch swapping; marginal stack-height cost; rare-but-real contact wear; bent-pin risk from careless removal. Right column ('soldered', neutral-outlined cards) lists: permanent low-failure-surface joint; no swapping without desoldering; zero tolerance for experimentation; one dead switch is a full repair job. Caption frames it as a genuine tradeoff rather than a one-sided win.
data_sources: hot-swap-sockets-tradeoffs.mdx § 'What the socket costs, physically' — 'A hot-swap socket sits proud of the PCB by roughly a millimeter or two...'; 'a socket connection... can, very slowly, loosen or develop contact resistance across years of insertion cycles...'; 'Pulling a switch out at an angle... can bend the socket's spring contact.'

hot-swap-sockets-tradeoffs.mdx § 'The soldered side of the ledger' — 'A soldered joint has a marginally lower failure surface than a socket... What a soldered PCB gives up in exchange is total: no swapping, no trying a new switch on a whim, no fixing one bad switch without an iron and a desoldering pump on hand. If a switch on a soldered board fails years into ownership... replacing it is a desoldering job.'
